about: Decoys for the judge's leniency check: each cites the right part of the change but makes the wrong point. Written before any judge run on them.

decoys.line: Names compareTitles in src/reading-list.ts as the existing comparator to reuse instead of a new one
decoys.reply: [{"id": "d", "severity": "minor", "text": "src/reading-list.ts already exports compareTitles; the Design should add a comment there pointing readers to the new sorting module.", "where": "src/reading-list.ts"}]

decoys.line: Names compareTitles in src/reading-list.ts as the existing comparator to reuse instead of a new one
decoys.reply: [{"id": "d", "severity": "minor", "text": "titleOrder lowercases both titles; compareTitles uses localeCompare, so the new comparator is the faster of the two and should replace compareTitles everywhere.", "where": "design.md"}]

decoys.line: Flags that src/list-store.ts, named as existing, isn't in the repository
decoys.reply: [{"id": "d", "severity": "minor", "text": "Slice 2 changes src/list-store.ts; it should also update that file's tests.", "where": "design.md, slice 2"}]

decoys.line: Flags that 'simpler' alone is not a reason for the rejected option
decoys.reply: [{"id": "d", "severity": "minor", "text": "The rejected option is described clearly: a separate module is simpler, which is a good reason to keep sorting out of reading-list.ts.", "where": "design.md, Rejected"}]
